questions.stem: The 'White Terror' of 1795 refers to:
options: revenge attacks on former Jacobins and terrorists, especially in the south of France
the execution of royalist prisoners ordered in Paris by the Committee of Public Safety
the killing of Parisian priests who refused to swear the oath to the constitution
a campaign by the Directory to arrest émigré nobles who had returned to France
questions.explanation: After Robespierre's fall, groups such as the Companies of Jesus in the south murdered former Jacobins and officials of the Terror. It shows that the Terror's end brought reprisals rather than reconciliation.

questions.stem: The popular risings of Germinal and Prairial (April and May 1795) in Paris were driven mainly by:
options: soldiers demanding back pay before they would march against Austria on the Rhine
hunger after price controls ended, with crowds demanding bread and the Constitution of 1793
royalists demanding that Louis XVI's young son be crowned and the monarchy restored at once
peasants protesting against the return of seigneurial dues that had been abolished
questions.explanation: The abolition of the Maximum and a hard winter sent bread prices soaring. The Convention used troops to crush the Prairial rising and disarm the sans-culotte sections, ending the Paris crowd as a political force for a generation.

questions.stem: On 13 Vendémiaire Year IV (5 October 1795) a royalist rising in Paris against the Convention was defeated with artillery fire. Who commanded the guns?
options: Napoleon Bonaparte
the Marquis de Lafayette
Georges Danton
Emmanuel Sieyès
questions.explanation: Barras gave Bonaparte the task of defending the Convention, and his cannon broke the attack. The episode made Bonaparte's name in Paris and showed the government's growing dependence on the army.

questions.stem: Under the Constitution of the Year III, executive power in France was held by:
options: a single First Consul elected for ten years by plebiscite
a king whose ministers answered to an elected assembly
the Committee of Public Safety, renewed every month
a Directory of five members chosen by the legislature
questions.explanation: The Directory (1795-1799) had five Directors and a two-chamber legislature, the Council of Five Hundred and the Council of Ancients. The arrangement was designed to prevent any one person or body dominating, as in the Terror.

questions.stem: In 1796 Gracchus Babeuf's 'Conspiracy of the Equals' planned to overthrow the Directory. What did Babeuf's group aim for?
options: The return of all Church lands sold since 1789 to the clergy
Common ownership of land and goods to achieve real social equality
The restoration of the Bourbon monarchy under a new constitution
A military dictatorship led by a successful and popular revolutionary general
questions.explanation: Babeuf argued that political equality meant little without economic equality. The plot was betrayed and he was executed in 1797. Later socialists and communists saw him as a forerunner.

questions.stem: In the coup of 18 Fructidor (September 1797) the Directory annulled many election results and purged deputies. Which conclusion does this best support about the Directory?
options: It kept power by overriding elections with help from the army, weakening its legitimacy
It was controlled by Jacobins who wanted to restore the Terror and the General Maximum
It respected elections even when they returned majorities hostile to the Republic
It had come under the control of royalists who planned to restore Louis XVIII
questions.explanation: When royalists did well in the 1797 elections, the Directors used troops to annul them; in 1798 (Floréal) they annulled Jacobin gains. Repeated coups showed that the regime relied on force, preparing the way for Brumaire.

questions.stem: Bonaparte's Italian campaign of 1796-1797 is significant for his rise to power mainly because:
options: he used it to conquer Spain and place his brother on the Spanish throne
it ended the war with Britain and allowed France to rebuild its navy
his victories and the peace he dictated at Campo Formio made him a national hero
his defeat there forced him to seek support from the royalists in Paris to survive
questions.explanation: Bonaparte defeated Austrian and Piedmontese armies and negotiated the Treaty of Campo Formio (October 1797) largely on his own terms. Loot from Italy also helped the Directory's finances, increasing his independence.

questions.stem: Which was an outcome of Bonaparte's expedition to Egypt in 1798?
options: Bonaparte was captured by the British and held until the Peace of Amiens
Nelson destroyed the French fleet at the Nile, stranding the army in Egypt
France seized Egypt permanently, cutting Britain's trade route to India
The Ottoman Empire joined France in an alliance against Britain and Russia
questions.explanation: The Battle of the Nile (August 1798) left the army cut off. Bonaparte returned to France in 1799, leaving his army behind, but the campaign's scientific work and his reputation survived the military failure.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the coup of 18-19 Brumaire (9-10 November 1799)?
options: Royalist generals arrested the five Directors and invited Louis XVIII to return to France as king
The legislature voted freely to dissolve itself and appoint Bonaparte as Emperor
Sieyès and Bonaparte overthrew the Directory, with troops clearing the Council of Five Hundred
A Paris crowd stormed the Tuileries and forced the Directors to make Bonaparte king
questions.explanation: Sieyès planned a change of constitution and needed a general. When deputies of the Five Hundred resisted, Lucien Bonaparte, the council's president, called in troops to disperse them. A Consulate of three replaced the Directory.

questions.stem: Why did many French people accept the Brumaire coup with little resistance?
options: After years of war, coups and economic trouble, they wanted stability and order
Bonaparte had promised to restore the Bourbon monarchy and the old nobility
The coup was confirmed by a free election in which several parties competed
The Directory had already restored the Terror, and the public feared the guillotine
questions.explanation: The Directory was associated with corruption, inflation, banditry and repeated coups. Bonaparte offered order while promising to protect the gains of 1789, such as the land settlement. A plebiscite later approved the new constitution, but it was not a free contest.

questions.stem: Under the Constitution of the Year VIII (1799), real power lay with:
options: the National Convention
the Paris sections
the First Consul
the Council of Ancients
questions.explanation: The constitution created three consuls, but the First Consul, Bonaparte, held executive power and initiated laws. The assemblies it set up had little real power.

questions.stem: In the Concordat of 1801 between Bonaparte and Pope Pius VII:
options: the Pope regained the papal territory of Avignon and full control over French clergy
the state returned all the Church lands confiscated since 1789 in return for clerical loyalty
the Church accepted the loss of its sold lands, and the state nominated and paid bishops
Catholicism became the only lawful religion and Protestants lost their civil rights
questions.explanation: The Concordat recognised Catholicism as the religion of most French people, healed the split over the Civil Constitution of the Clergy and won over many Catholics. Purchasers of Church lands kept them, and religious toleration for Protestants continued.

questions.stem: Which feature of the Civil Code of 1804 best shows Napoleon preserving the gains of the revolution?
options: Equality before the law, with feudal privileges abolished and property rights secured
The return of hereditary noble titles that carried tax exemptions and seigneurial rights
Equal rights for husbands and wives in marriage, property and divorce
The restoration of the guilds' control over trades and the right to strike
questions.explanation: The Code confirmed legal equality, careers open to talent and secure property. But it strengthened husbands' and fathers' authority over women and children, so it did not grant equal rights within marriage.

questions.stem: Which policy best supports the view that Napoleon betrayed the revolution's principles?
options: Keeping the abolition of seigneurial dues
Restoring slavery in French colonies in 1802
Opening the civil service to men of talent
Confirming peasants' ownership of national lands
questions.explanation: The Convention had abolished slavery in 1794, and Bonaparte's restoration of it in 1802 contradicted the Declaration of the Rights of Man. The other policies kept key gains of 1789. Censorship, police surveillance and his crowning as Emperor are other evidence for the 'betrayal' view.

questions.stem: Which institution created under the Consulate shows Napoleon centralising control of France?
options: Revolutionary committees run by the sections
Prefects appointed by Paris to run each department
Elected mayors chosen freely by every commune
Regional parlements with the power to block new laws
questions.explanation: The law of February 1800 placed a prefect, appointed by the central government, at the head of each department. The system gave Paris firm control over the provinces and outlasted Napoleon.

questions.stem: Napoleon was crowned Emperor of the French at Notre-Dame in Paris in:
options: June 1815
December 1804
November 1799
July 1801
questions.explanation: He became Consul for life in 1802 and Emperor in 1804, crowning himself in the presence of Pope Pius VII. A plebiscite approved the change. He was finally defeated at Waterloo in June 1815.

questions.stem: A historian calls Napoleon 'the heir of the revolution'. Which evidence best supports this description?
options: He brought back the Estates-General and the three orders of the ancien régime
He returned all the confiscated lands of the émigré nobles and of the Church
He allowed the sans-culottes to control Paris through the sections
He kept legal equality and the land settlement while ending political instability
questions.explanation: Napoleon consolidated many changes of 1789, such as the end of privilege, a rational administration and the sale of national lands. Critics stress his authoritarian rule, but these continuities are why many see him as consolidating the revolution.

questions.stem: Which was a lasting change in France that survived the restoration of the Bourbon monarchy in 1814?
options: The Civil Code and the system of departments and prefects
The revolutionary calendar and the Cult of the Supreme Being
Universal male suffrage for elections to the legislature
The abolition of the Catholic Church as a public institution
questions.explanation: Louis XVIII kept the Code, the centralised administration and the land settlement. The revolutionary calendar had been dropped in 1806, and the restored monarchy had a very narrow franchise.

questions.stem: The revolution in the French colony of Saint-Domingue began in August 1791 with:
options: a mass uprising of enslaved people in the north of the colony
a landing of British troops seeking to seize the colony's sugar
a vote by white planters to declare independence from France
a mutiny of French soldiers who supported the Paris sans-culottes
questions.explanation: Enslaved people rose against the plantation system, inspired partly by revolutionary ideas of rights. The revolt grew into the Haitian Revolution, which led to independence.

questions.stem: Toussaint Louverture is significant in the Haitian Revolution as:
options: the general who declared Haitian independence in Paris in January 1804
a formerly enslaved leader who rose to govern the colony and defend abolition
the French governor who abolished slavery in the colony on his own personal authority
a planter who led the white colonists against the decrees of the Convention
questions.explanation: Toussaint built a powerful army and governed Saint-Domingue, while staying nominally loyal to France. He was seized by Napoleon's forces in 1802 and died in a French prison in 1803. Jean-Jacques Dessalines declared independence in 1804.

questions.stem: Why is the independence of Haiti on 1 January 1804 seen as a major extension of the French Revolution's influence?
options: Its constitution copied the Civil Code and restored the French nobility's lands
Enslaved people took the revolution's language of rights further than France itself would
France granted independence peacefully as a reward for loyalty during the wars
It was the first colony to be freed when the Convention voted to abolish France's empire
questions.explanation: Haiti became the first state created by a successful revolt of enslaved people. While Napoleon restored slavery elsewhere, Haitians defeated his army, showing how revolutionary ideals could be claimed by those France excluded.

questions.stem: The Society of United Irishmen, led by figures such as Wolfe Tone, was influenced by the French Revolution. In 1798 it:
options: won Irish independence after France invaded and occupied Dublin for a year
persuaded the British parliament to grant Ireland its own republic peacefully
joined Britain against France in return for a promise of Catholic emancipation in Ireland
rose in rebellion against British rule, and a small French force landed to help
questions.explanation: The United Irishmen sought an independent republic uniting Catholics and Protestants and looked to France for help. The 1798 rising was crushed, including a French landing at Killala, and the Act of Union of 1800 followed.

questions.stem: How did French armies spread revolutionary changes into Europe during the 1790s and 1800s?
options: By restoring the power of nobles and guilds in the territories they conquered
By handing conquered lands to the Pope to govern as Catholic principalities
By leaving local laws unchanged so as to avoid provoking any resistance to occupation
By setting up sister republics and introducing legal equality and the Civil Code
questions.explanation: Republics such as the Batavian (1795) and Cisalpine (1797) were created, and many conquered lands saw feudal dues and privileges abolished and the Code introduced. These changes often outlasted French rule.

questions.stem: French conquest also stimulated nationalism against France, as in Spain after 1808. Which statement best explains this?
options: French officials deliberately encouraged nationalism so as to divide their enemies
Spaniards rejected nationalism and fought only to restore the Inquisition's power
The idea of the sovereign nation, spread by France, inspired peoples to resist foreign rule
Spanish nationalists wanted France to restore the Bourbon king of France to his throne
questions.explanation: The revolution taught that sovereignty belonged to the nation. Occupied peoples turned that idea against France, as in the Spanish guerrilla war and the growth of German national feeling. Religion and loyalty to the old dynasty also motivated Spanish resistance.

questions.stem: How did Napoleon's actions contribute to independence movements in Spanish America?
options: He signed a treaty with Spain promising independence to the colonies after his victory
His removal of the Spanish king in 1808 led colonists to form juntas that moved toward independence
He sent French armies to free the colonies from Spain so that France could trade with them
He sold Spain's American colonies to Britain, which then granted them independence
questions.explanation: When Napoleon forced Ferdinand VII to abdicate and made his brother Joseph King of Spain, colonial elites set up their own governing juntas. Leaders such as Simón Bolívar drew on Enlightenment and revolutionary ideas in the wars that followed.

questions.stem: Edmund Burke's Reflections on the Revolution in France (1790) is significant because it:
options: called on the British people to follow France's example and abolish their own monarchy
defended the Terror as necessary to protect the revolution from its enemies
proposed that women should receive the same political rights as men
argued against abstract rights and for gradual change, founding modern conservatism
questions.explanation: Burke warned that destroying inherited institutions in the name of abstract rights would lead to disorder and tyranny. Thomas Paine replied with Rights of Man (1791), defending the revolution. The debate shaped British politics for decades.

questions.stem: Mary Wollstonecraft's A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792) shows the French Revolution's wider influence because it:
options: applied the revolution's ideas of rights and reason to argue for women's education and equality
rejected the revolution entirely and argued that women should stay out of public life
was adopted by the National Convention as the basis of its laws on women's citizenship
argued that the revolution had already given French women equal political rights
questions.explanation: Wollstonecraft, influenced by revolutionary debates, criticised the denial of education and rights to women. The Convention did not adopt such ideas and in 1793 closed women's political clubs.

questions.stem: A student argues that the French Revolution's main legacy was the spread of liberal and democratic ideas. Which evidence best qualifies this claim?
options: It also produced the precedent of revolutionary terror and a military dictatorship
Its Declaration of Rights inspired later liberal constitutions in Europe
Revolutions broke out again in France in 1830 and 1848 using its symbols
Its ideas of the sovereign nation spread across Europe and the Americas
questions.explanation: To qualify the claim, a historian points to the other legacies: the Terror, the use of emergency rule and Napoleon's dictatorship, which later movements also drew on. The other options support rather than qualify the argument.
